 Ashok Kumar Hasani

High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Jabalpur

sentences.text: Shri Amit Pandey - Panel Lawyer for State.

Order 
This petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure has been filed challenging the order dated 25.01.2019 passed in CRR/44/2018 by the learned Sessions Judge, Harda, District Harda affirming the order dated 02.11.2018 passed in RCT No.198 of 2011, by the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Harda whereby the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Harda dismissed the application filed under Sections 227, 245 and 228 of the Cr.P.C.
2.

The case of the applicant is that the respondent herein has filed a complaint against the applicant before the learned trial Court for the offences punishable under Sections 7(1), 7(v) Rule 50 read with Section 16(a)(i) and 16(1)(a)(ii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 alleging therein that on 26.07.2008 at about 01:00 PM Smt. Adlin E. Panna has inspected the shop of the applicant situated near Ghantaghar Chowk, Harda, District Harda.
The applicant is the proprietor of the shop.

In presence of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:56979 2 MCRC-8181-2019 independent witness collected sample of food material and has packed the sample of Vimal Pouch and Kali Mirch and thereafter sent the same for examination before the laboratory.
The Food Inspector has found that the food stuff collected is of substandard quality, therefore, a complaint was preferred on 18.03.2011, which is registered as Criminal Case No.198 of 2011.

3. TIn support of the complaint the authority has examined witness before the learned Judicial Ashok Kumar Hasani vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10658843/
1 Magistrate First Class, Harda.

sentences.text: The applicant filed application under Sections 227, 245 and 228 of the Cr.P.C. before the learned trial Court on the ground that the complaint against the applicant is based upon the technical grounds whereas there are special provisions for filing complaint which was not followed by the prescribed officer and without taking the report to the competent authority under Section 13(2) of the Act the complaint was filed.
No proper procedure has been followed by respondent as the sample has been collected by the Food Inspector Adlin E. Panna and the complaint has been filed by the Food Inspector Shakuntala Mishra.
The sample was collected before two and a half years, therefore, the complaint itself is not maintainable.
The said application was rejected by the learned Judicial Magistrate on 02.11.2018.
The revision preferred against the same has also been dismissed vide order dated 25.01.2019.
Against which the present petition has been filed on the ground that both the Courts have not considered the grounds raised in the application in proper perspective.

The sample were collected on 26.07.2008 at about 03:30 PM and the complaint has been preferred against the applicant on 18.03.2011 with a NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-JBP:56979 3 MCRC-8181-2019 delay of nearly about two and a half years and there is no explanation for the delay in filing the complaint.

The other ground raised is that the report was received on 26.08.2008 and without discussion with the superior authorities the permission was granted on 16.03.2011.There is nothing on record to explain the delay in filing the complaint.
No proper opportunity of hearing was granted to the accused/applicant during the proceedings.
He is not the manufacturer of the Vimal Pouch, therefore, he cannot be made an accused.
The complaint was instituted nearly two and a half years after obtaining the sample.
The shelf life of the article was only six months, thereafter, how the complaint is still maintainable has not been considered by the learned trial Court.

Learned counsel for the applicant has placed reliance upon a judgment passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Municipal Corporation of Delhi vs Ghisa Ram, AIR 1967 SC 970 and the judgment passed by this Court in the case of Prakash Desai and another vs.
State of M.P., 2015 (3) JLJ 439 and has prayed for quashment of the entire proceedings.

sentences.text: 4. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of State has opposed the arguments and supported the impugned order.
It is submitted that the scope of interference in cognizance matter is limited.

The main defence of the applicant is put-forth to get the application for discharge allowed that is not permissible in view of the judgment passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, which was considered by the learned trial Court as well as the revisional Court.
If some mistake has been committed by the authorities during investigation or collection of sample the accused cannot get the benefit at this stage.

It has to be seen by the learned trial Court at the later stage that NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-JBP:56979 4 MCRC-8181-2019 cannot be a sole ground for discharging the accused from the criminal prosecution.
His statement, which has been recorded before the trial Court clearly established that a prima facie case is made out against the present applicant.

There is a dispute with respect to collection of samples and samples were sent to the laboratory for examination and after due examination finding the sample to be substandard the complaint can always be filed by the authorities.
The learned trial Court as well as the learned revisional Court have not committed any error in rejecting the application filed by the applicant.
5. This petition is pending since 2019.
No interim relief has been granted by this Court at any point of time.

The order sheet dated 19.02.2024 shows that the original record was received before this Court, therefore, no proceedings are undertaken by the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class,

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This Court returned back the original record and directed the trial Court to proceed in the matter.
6. Looking to the overall facts and circumstances of the case coupled with the report of the public analyst wherein the said Vimal Gutka pouch was found to be of substandard.
The learned trial Court was well within its jurisdiction and has taken cognizance in the matter and has rightly rejected the application.
The case law which has been relied upon is of no help to the applicant specifically for the reason that there is no substantial delay in collection of sample and sent the same for forensic analysis.
The delay is in filing the complaint, therefore, the fact that the sample become decomposed or expired will not be of any help to the applicant.

Under these NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-JBP:56979 5 MCRC-8181-2019 circumstances, no relief can be extended to the applicant.
7. The petition sans merit and is accordingly dismissed.

(VISHAL MISHRA) JUDGE THK Ashok Kumar Hasani vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10658843/
